title: Micro-batching + KV shadow rollout — weekly scramble
content:
Meeting: Serving Runtime weekly sync — micro-batching + KV shadow (informal)
Date: 2027-10-18
Attendees: Priya Menon (owner), Liam Chen, Ava Thompson, Diego Ramirez, Zoe Patel, Maya Singh
Location: Zoom + #serving-runtime

TL;DR:
- Rolled KV shadow reads to 5% of production traffic for the micro-batch path; initial results are promising (p99 token latency reduced ~8% on routing tier).
- Micro-batching shim prototype landed in branch 'microbatch-shim-v2' (PR 4271). Needs perf regression checks against long-seq workloads.
- Kernel team validated a SIMD-friendly attention kernel change that reduces GEMM overhead in short-context cases; still working through thread-local memory churn.
- Several follow-ups (timeouts, metrics gaps, QA plan) — see action items.

Observations / Metrics:
- Baseline (no shadow): avg token latency = 18.4ms, p95 = 42ms, p99 = 110ms (mixed host of 16GB-a100 nodes).
- Shadow traffic (5%) on micro-batch path: avg = 17.6ms, p95 = 39ms, p99 = 101ms. Note: numbers are noisy due to traffic bursts at 03:00 UTC.
- KV cache hit rate unchanged at ~72% overall; when micro-batched, effective per-request KV lookups reduced by ~12% because of prefix coalescing.
- Cost proxy (tokens/sec per GPU): +3.5% improvement observed in the shadowed cohort so far.

Kernel work (notes):
- Liam: SIMD attention patch (local branch 'simd-attn-lite') reduces per-token CPU overhead for 1-8 token steps. Benchmarks show 6-9% speedup for short completion lengths on CPU fallback.
  - Outstanding: thread-local page allocations spike under synthetic churn (~1% throughput loss under pathological reentry). Need to add pooling.
  - Action: Liam -> add simple arena allocator to patch and run perf regression suite (INF-4820).

KV cache details and rollout plan:
- Approach: Shadow reads write to new 'microbatch-kv' cache namespace but do not affect production caches. We compare hit rates and false positive/consistency metrics.
- Current state: Shadow read injector at ingress, collates prefixes for 10ms window (configurable). Works for both streaming and non-streaming.
- Observed benefit: For multi-turn chat traffic, coalescing reduced duplicate KV fetches by ~18% on average.
- Concern: Under extremely bursty workloads the coalescer introduces ~3–4ms scheduling jitter for the request that triggers the coalescing window.
  - Mitigation idea: dynamic window shrinkage based on backlog and per-instance CPU headroom.

Batching and routing heuristics:
- Micro-batch shim behavior: small hold window (3–10ms) to allow coalescing while prioritizing latency-sensitive short requests. Tunable per-model.
- Bucketed batching experiment: separate queue for <64-token vs >=64-token sequences; this reduces head-of-line blocking in tests.
- Canary config: per-model override to disable microbatch shim for models with strict p99 SLOs. Useful for enterprise customers with pinned latency.

Incidents / Bugs discovered this week:
- PR 4271 uncovered a GC pause on envoy sidecar when running the shim under high QPS in staging -> traced to large proto allocs in debug logging path.
  - Fix: Ava to submit a small PR to reduce logging payloads and move heavy debug logs behind a flag. Target: 2027-10-21.
- Repro: intermittent KV cache inconsistency for keys with long prefixes when coalescer merges hits; appears in ~0.02% of shadowed requests.
  - Hypothesis: race between async writeback and shadow read query.
  - Action: Diego -> write small fuzz test and a reproducible harness (JIRA-INF-4913).

Decisions made:
- Continue shadow rollout to 10% if no regressions by next Wednesday (2027-10-25).
- Keep micro-batch shim default enabled in staging but disabled by default in enterprise prod until we have per-route safety gates.
- Kernel changes that touch memory alloc patterns must include allocation telemetry and an opt-out config flag.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Liam Chen: Add arena allocator to simd-attn-lite branch and run perf suite (INF-4820). ETA: 2027-10-22.
- Ava Thompson: Reduce debug logging payloads for shim path and create canary build. PR -> target 4279. ETA: 2027-10-21.
- Diego Ramirez: Build fuzz harness for long-prefix KV inconsistency and file a clear reproduction ticket (INF-4913). ETA: 2027-10-20.
- Zoe Patel: Update rollout dashboard to include coalescer-induced jitter and per-instance headroom. ETA: 2027-10-24.
- Maya Singh: QA plan for microbatch shim across streaming/non-streaming; include load test matrix and p99 regression thresholds. ETA: 2027-10-26.

Risks and open questions:
- How to attribute cost savings precisely when micro-batching interacts with GPU kernel fusion? We need a clearer cost model (tokens/GPU-second per config).
- Is dynamic window shrinkage susceptible to oscillation under mixed workloads? Need slow-control simulation.
- Should we persist microbatch coalescer metrics to longer retention for retrospective analysis? Currently 7d only.

Notes to self / informal brainstorms:
- Consider a hybrid approach: aggressive coalescing for warm clients (session affinity) but conservative for anonymous short bursts.
- Could use a lightweight per-VM token bucket to gate coalescer window based on recent tail latency.
- Idea: expose a per-route 'microbatch_profile' that contains min_hold_ms, max_hold_ms, and backlog_thresholds for fine tuning by product owners.

Next week focus (prioritized):
1) Fix allocator + smoke test (Liam).
2) Reproduce and fix KV inconsistency (Diego).
3) Push shadow to 10% and monitor p99 drift closely (Priya + Zoe).
4) QA matrix + canary builds for enterprise (Maya + Ava).

Misc notes / links:
- Latest perf dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/serving-runtime/microbatch-kv
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4271
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345678
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/thread/FGH12345

End of notes.

Quick checklist before next sync:
- [ ] Perf regression suite green on simd-attn-lite
- [ ] Repro for KV inconsistency
- [ ] Canary build with reduced logging
- [ ] Dashboard tile for coalescer jitter added

Unresolved: Should we include a short A/B for bucket thresholds (32/64/128) or just stick to 64 split? Put on agenda for Wed tech sync.
